claude.rationale: gap_45=1: the customer-facing productive asset (new-build Permian processing capacity) crossed into split 50/50 co-ownership, but the processes that build and run it did NOT cross to a shared operator — "Crosstex will manage construction and operate the facilities," so ownership of the product was split while the operating processes remained solely with the Partnership, a product-vs-process mismatch at closing. The gap was contractually bridged by the Credit Agreement Amendment (lien accommodation on the co-owned assets and increased JV investment capacity), supporting gap_mitigated=yes. gap_56=0: no operational process was re-engineered or transferred away from the organization that runs it — process (T5) and organization/people (T6) both stayed intact with Crosstex, and "no transfer of management or workforce is described," so there is no process-vs-organization mismatch. This is a joint-interest co-ownership of a single new asset (imprint-share), not a transfer of business model, entity, or people, hence those tiers are null.

gemini.rationale: The deal involves a 50/50 joint investment in a new-build processing facility (T4), creating a shared ownership structure (T1 imprint-share). However, Crosstex alone manages construction and operates the facilities (T5), meaning the operational processes did not cross to a shared operator, creating a gap_45. There is no gap_56 because Crosstex retained both the operations (T5) and the organization/people (T6) to run them. The gap is mitigated by the joint interest arrangement and lien accommodations.

openai.rationale: The slice states that the new processing capacity was split into 50% working interests, while "Crosstex will manage construction and operate the facilities," documenting a product-versus-process ownership mismatch at closing and supporting gap_45=1. It also states that no management or workforce transferred and that Crosstex supplied both the operating processes and the operating organization, so those tiers remained coherently together and gap_56=0. The cited contractual bridge consisted of lien accommodation and credit-facility investment changes, not a documented transitional-services or operating agreement absorbing the gap.
